title: Launch V-Vault from the dev Portal
preconditions: A valid plusproject Portal account with V-Vault enabled.
steps:
1. Open the dev Portal and sign in.
2. Click the V-Vault tile.
3. Check the browser tab title and the address bar.
expected:
1. V-Vault opens on the public dev V-Vault host with a signed-in session.
2. The tab title uses V-Vault and the company legal name.
3. There is no V-Vault email or password form for staff.
4. The launch code is exchanged once and does not stay on the URL.

title: A direct visit or deep link works while already signed in
preconditions: A signed-in V-Vault session in the same browser.
steps:
1. With a session already open, visit the V-Vault home URL directly.
2. Open a deep link to My Vault (/files) and to Transfer Center (/transfers).
expected:
1. Home, My Vault and Transfer Center open without asking the person to sign in again.
2. The session stays on the public dev host.

title: Employee sidebar shows work pages and no admin tools
preconditions: A signed-in employee who is not a company admin.
steps:
1. List every sidebar item.
2. Confirm My Vault, Secure Transfer, Transfer Center, Secure Intake, Email outbox and Recovery are present.
3. Confirm Audit Trail, Scan log and Sharing Policy are not offered.
expected:
1. The employee sidebar shows the work pages, including Email outbox, and uses the label My Vault.
2. Admin-only tools (Audit Trail, Scan log, Sharing Policy) are not in the sidebar.

title: Admin sidebar includes Audit Trail, Scan log and Sharing Policy
preconditions: A signed-in company admin.
steps:
1. List every sidebar item, including the admin section.
2. Open Audit Trail, Scan log and Sharing Policy.
expected:
1. The admin sidebar includes Audit Trail, Scan log and Sharing Policy, plus the staff work pages.
2. Each of those three admin pages opens.

title: Open My Vault and read list, columns, search and quota
preconditions: A signed-in employee with at least one file or folder. An empty user is useful for the empty state.
steps:
1. Open My Vault from the sidebar or from Open My Vault on Home.
2. Check type, size and date columns, the quota bar, and the scan status column (scanning is on in this environment).
3. Use breadcrumbs and the folder tree.
4. Search or filter for a known file.
5. If the list is empty, confirm the empty state. After a refresh, confirm a loading skeleton appears briefly.
expected:
1. My Vault opens and lists only this person's items.
2. Columns, quota and scan status are correct.
3. Breadcrumbs, tree and search work.
4. Empty and loading states use hub moments or skeletons, not a raw blank page.

title: Create, rename, move and delete a folder, including validation and cancel
preconditions: A signed-in employee who can create folders in My Vault.
steps:
1. Create a uniquely named folder.
2. Try a duplicate name and a blank name.
3. Rename the folder, including special characters.
4. Move the folder to another parent.
5. Open create, rename or move and cancel without saving.
6. Delete the folder to Recovery.
expected:
1. A unique folder is created. Duplicate and blank names are refused.
2. Rename, special characters and move work.
3. Cancel leaves the tree unchanged.
4. Delete sends the folder to Recovery. Success or error uses a hub toast. Dialogs are standard hub dialogs.
testData: New folder names you can tidy up afterwards

title: Open Secure Transfer, pick content and recipients, and leave without sending
preconditions: A signed-in employee with an owned file or folder, and an outside email.
steps:
1. Open Secure Transfer.
2. Confirm there is no Security controls or malware-posture panel on this page (those panels were removed).
3. Add recipients as email chips and pick files or folders from My Vault.
4. Check the preview card.
5. Try to send with no files picked, then leave or refresh before sending.
expected:
1. The page opens with the current copy (Private links. Email confirmation. You stay in control.).
2. There is no separate Security controls or malware-posture summary panel.
3. Recipients, picks and the preview card work. Send is blocked until at least one file or folder is picked.
4. Leaving before send does not create a transfer.
testData: Owned file or folder; outside email

title: Send with View and download, several files, subject, message and default alerts
preconditions: A signed-in employee, two owned files, and an outside recipient you can reach (or Email outbox).
steps:
1. Send two or more files, access set to View and download, with a Subject (required) and an optional message.
2. Confirm default access alerts are on unless you turned them off.
3. After send, check the success moment and Transfer Center.
4. Confirm the optional message is not shown to the guest until after the code is accepted.
5. If mail is local only, confirm the form hint points the sender to Email outbox.
expected:
1. The transfer is created and listed. Subject is required (for example Q3 drawings).
2. Default alerts are on. A hub success moment appears after send.
3. The optional message is visible to the guest only after the code.
4. When mail is local only, the form tells the sender to use Email outbox.

title: Open Transfer Center, filter, search and read status
preconditions: A signed-in employee with at least one send and, if possible, one request.
steps:
1. Open Transfer Center.
2. Filter or tab by kind and status, and confirm request rows are distinct from send rows.
3. Search for a known transfer.
4. Check status badges and the protection column (view only, watermark).
5. Confirm you only see your own transfers.
6. After a guest opens a transfer, refresh the list.
expected:
1. The list opens and can be filtered and searched.
2. Sends and requests are distinct. Badges and the protection column are accurate.
3. An employee only sees their own transfers. A refresh after a guest open updates activity or status.
4. The empty state is a hub empty state.

title: Transfer detail: files, activity, inbound, expiry and the sender's own copy
preconditions: A signed-in employee with a send, a request with inbound files if possible, and if possible an expired transfer.
steps:
1. Open a transfer from the list.
2. Check the file list, per-person activity and the audit trail on the detail.
3. On a request, open inbound files.
4. Download the sender's own copy if that control is offered.
5. Open an expired transfer and confirm it is read-only.
expected:
1. Detail opens with the correct transfer.
2. File list, per-person activity and the audit trail are accurate for this transfer only.
3. Inbound files on a request can be opened by the owner.
4. An expired transfer is read-only unless the product clearly offers extend.
testData: Owned send; optional request and expired transfer

title: Open a valid invite, enter the code, and read the transfer subject heading
preconditions: A valid send invite for an outside address you can read (or Email outbox). Use a private window.
steps:
1. Open the invite link in a private window.
2. Confirm the link does not include a company id, and that the masked email hint matches the invited address.
3. Request a code, read it, and enter the correct 6-digit code.
4. Confirm guest branding belongs to the sending company.
5. After the transfer opens, find the kicker labelled Secure Transfer (it may display as SECURE TRANSFER) and read the main heading directly under it.
expected:
1. The guest door opens from the sealed invite link (no company id in the URL).
2. The masked email hint matches the invited address. The correct code signs the guest in to that transfer only.
3. Branding is the sending company's branding and does not leak another company.
4. The main heading under the Secure Transfer kicker is the transfer subject: the same Subject the sender typed on the Secure Transfer form (the field labelled Subject). It is not a separate title field, and it is not the transfer id unless the sender used that as the subject.
testData: Valid invite; readable mailbox or outbox

title: Wrong, short, expired and reused codes, and the five-attempt lock
preconditions: A valid test invite and a private window. Do not lock a production guest you still need.
steps:
1. Enter a wrong 6-digit code, then a code that is not six digits.
2. Enter a wrong code five times and confirm this code is locked.
3. Confirm a used or old code cannot be reused.
4. If you can wait for the code lifetime (15 minutes), confirm an expired code is refused.
expected:
1. A wrong code is refused. A code that is not six digits is refused.
2. Five wrong attempts lock this code.
3. A used or expired code cannot be reused. Messages do not leak whether other invites exist.

title: Activity log: open, filter, contents and empty state
preconditions: A company admin session. Recent sends, opens, downloads or rule changes help.
steps:
1. Open Audit Trail.
2. Filter by who, dates and action.
3. Confirm the log includes opens, downloads, sends and rule changes when those events have happened.
4. Apply a filter that matches nothing.
expected:
1. The Activity log opens for a company admin.
2. Filters work. Expected event kinds appear for this company only.
3. A no-match filter shows a clear empty state.

title: Activity export, integrity check and tenant isolation are admin-only
preconditions: A company admin and an employee. A second tenant is optional.
steps:
1. As an employee, try to open Activity, export CSV and run the integrity check.
2. As an admin, export the log as CSV and run the integrity check.
3. Confirm the on-screen log and the CSV do not include another company.
expected:
1. An employee cannot use the company Activity log, export or integrity check.
2. An admin can read, export and verify the log.
3. The log and the CSV do not include another company or tenant.
testData: Admin and employee; optional second tenant

title: Email outbox: open, kinds, empty state and own-mail only
preconditions: Live mail may be off, so use Email outbox. An employee session, and some invites, codes or alerts if they exist.
steps:
1. Open Email outbox from the main sidebar (it is a staff work page, not an admin-only tool).
2. Confirm you only see your own outbound mail.
3. Confirm invite, code and alert kinds are listed when they exist, and check the empty state if there is no mail.
4. Confirm secret links or codes are not casually exposed in a shared list. Record the actual behaviour.
expected:
1. Email outbox opens from the main sidebar for an employee.
2. An employee does not see other people's outbound mail.
3. Invite, code and alert kinds appear when they exist. The empty state is a hub empty state.
4. Secret links are not casually exposed.
testData: Employee; existing outbound items if any

title: Admin outbox scope
preconditions: A company admin session, plus outbound mail from at least one other person if it exists.
steps:
1. Open Email outbox as an admin.
2. Record whether the admin sees only their own mail, or company mail, and write that rule in Remarks.
expected:
1. Email outbox opens.
2. Admin scope matches the product rule. Record that rule.

title: Storage links, honest encryption reporting, complete download and replace
preconditions: A signed-in admin or employee who owns a file. Do not paste bucket names, keys or signed URLs into this workbook.
steps:
1. Upload or open a file and confirm a complete download matches the upload.
2. Confirm download links use a short lifetime (from product docs or a safe status screen, not by spreading a signed URL).
3. If security status is available to a signed-in admin through a safe API or screen, confirm the encryption flag is honest. Do not expect a Security controls panel on Sharing Policy or Secure Transfer (those panels were removed).
4. Replace or re-upload over an existing file if the product allows it, and confirm the change is not silent.
expected:
1. Download is complete and matches the upload.
2. Download links are short-lived; do not copy the URL into this file.
3. The encryption flag, if shown, is honest. There is no Security controls posture panel on Send or Sharing Policy.
4. Replacing a file is visible (new version, toast, or a refused duplicate), never a silent overwrite.

title: Scanning: health, clean files, a blocked test file, guest uploads and scan status
preconditions: The live dev API currently reports scanning as clamav. A clean file, and only the company's approved harmless scanner test file if policy allows it.
steps:
1. Open the direct dev API /health and confirm scanning is reported (currently clamav). scanning_warning should be absent while scanning is on.
2. Upload and send a clean file, then open it as the guest.
3. If policy allows, try the approved harmless scanner test file and confirm it cannot leave the company.
4. If a scan-required setting is on, confirm an unscanned or blocked file cannot be sent.
5. Upload as a guest to a request and confirm the upload is scanned.
6. Confirm scan status is visible on My Vault and on transfer files, and that Scan log records the event for an admin.
expected:
1. Health reports the scanner in use and does not leak secrets.
2. A clean file can be sent and opened.
3. The approved test file, if used, is blocked or rejected and cannot leave the company. Never use a real harmful sample.
4. Guest uploads are scanned. Scan status is visible on transfer files too. Scan log shows metadata only.
testData: Clean file; optional approved test file; request invite

title: Portal branding, typography, wordmarks, emails and plain language
preconditions: Portal admin access to Branding. Restore values after. Check several V-Vault screens plus a guest page and an email.
steps:
1. Confirm colours, fonts, typography, logo, favicon and header chrome come from Portal Branding.
2. Publish a safe temporary Branding change, confirm V-Vault picks it up (including when you return to the tab), then restore.
3. Confirm other hub wordmarks are not used as the V-Vault or company logo, and that no off-brand font or colour appears.
4. Confirm emails pick up the logo and brand colour.
5. Read the copy on Scan log, Email outbox, session-ended and Home and confirm plain language, including the My Vault label.
expected:
1. Colours, fonts, typography, logo, favicon and header chrome come from Portal Branding.
2. A Branding publish is picked up, then original values are restored.
3. Other hub wordmarks are not used as the V-Vault logo.
4. Emails pick up logo and brand colour. New and updated screens use plain language and the My Vault label.
testData: Portal Branding access; one email sample

title: Hub toasts and standard hub dialogs on every V-Vault action
preconditions: A signed-in staff user who can trigger a success, an error, and at least one dialog (delete, move, stop sharing).
steps:
1. Trigger a success and an error (for example a good upload and a refused type).
2. Open a dialog, confirm title and X, footer buttons on the right, and that Esc closes it.
expected:
1. Every success or error message is a hub toast. A green pill-shaped message is a Fail.
2. Every popup is a standard hub dialog (title plus X, footer buttons on the right, Esc closes).
testData: Any file action that shows a toast and a dialog

title: Role permissions: own files, staff routes, and guest limits
preconditions: An employee, a company admin, and a guest session on a transfer or request.
steps:
1. As an employee, create, upload, rename, move and delete your own files.
2. Confirm staff routes (My Vault, transfers, usage, profile, branding) require a signed-in staff session.
3. As a guest, try to list My Vault items and staff transfers.
4. From a private window with no session, try to change data (create a transfer or edit a folder) and confirm it is refused.
expected:
1. An employee can manage their own files.
2. Staff routes require a session.
3. A guest session cannot list My Vault and cannot list staff transfers.
4. Requests without a session cannot change data.

title: Public health is safe; security headers, cookies and branding APIs
preconditions: Use the direct dev API host for /health (the Vercel frontend does not proxy /health). A signed-in staff session is also needed for branding. Do not paste cookie values into this workbook.
steps:
1. Open the direct dev API /health without a session and read the body.
2. Inspect security headers on health and on a 401 staff route (V-Vault host /v1/auth/me or the same path on the direct API host).
3. In DevTools, confirm session cookies are httpOnly and not readable by page script. Do not copy cookie values.
4. Call /v1/branding and /v1/theme without a session, then with a staff session, using the V-Vault host.
expected:
1. Health is public. The body includes status, a service name, and scanning (currently clamav). scanning_warning appears only when scanning is off. The body does not leak secrets.
2. Security headers are present on API responses. The public Vercel host also sends HSTS.
3. Cookies are httpOnly and not exposed to script.
4. Branding and theme APIs require a staff session.
testData: Direct dev API /health; Vercel same-origin /v1; staff session; DevTools

title: Existing plusproject data still opens after the latest deploy
preconditions: Known plusproject files and transfers from before this test run, on the deployed dev environment.
steps:
1. Open several existing plusproject files in My Vault.
2. Open several existing transfers.
3. Refresh Sharing Policy and Audit Trail (as admin) and confirm they still work.
4. Confirm /health on the direct dev API and the V-Vault frontend still answer.
expected:
1. Existing files and transfers still open.
2. Rules and audit still work after a refresh.
3. Health and the UI still answer after the latest deploy.

title: Demo path: launch, branding, Home, My Vault, send, guest, request and audit
preconditions: A company admin, a clean PDF, an outside recipient you can read, and Activity access.
steps:
1. Launch V-Vault from the dev Portal and confirm branding and Home stats.
2. Upload or pick a file in My Vault and send it to the outside recipient, with a clear Subject.
3. Open the guest door, enter the code, confirm the heading under the Secure Transfer kicker is that Subject, and view the file.
4. Create a short file request.
5. Open Audit Trail and Email outbox and confirm the send and related events.
expected:
1. The demo path works end to end on the deployed dev URLs without a blocker.
2. Branding is correct, Home stats load, the guest sees only that transfer and the correct subject heading, and Activity and Email outbox record the send.
3. This is a client-handover path; any Fail here is P1.
